claim: Official docs: test trigger and behavior separately via a with-skill/without-skill baseline in a fresh session; skill-creator description-tuning, troubleshooting over-triggering, /doctor, 1536-char cap.
quote: Seeing a skill trigger tells you Claude found it, not that it did what you intended. To know a skill is working, measure two things separately: whether Claude invokes it on the prompts it should, and whether the output matches what you expect when it does.

claim: Agent Skills standard: evals.json schema, with-skill vs without-skill runs, assertions, grading.json/timing.json/benchmark.json delta, snapshot baseline via cp -r, blind comparison, iteration-N dirs.
quote: The core pattern is to run each test case twice: once with the skill and once without it (or with a previous version). This gives you a baseline to compare against.

claim: skill-creator eval/description-tuning upgrade shipped March 3 2026; analyzes description against sample prompts to cut false positives and false negatives; improved triggering on 5 of 6 public skills.
quote: analyzes your current description against sample prompts and suggests edits that cut both false positives and false negatives ... we ran it across our document-creation skills and saw improved triggering on 5 out of 6 public skills.

claim: MLflow CI harness: YAML config drives headless Claude Code, traces tool calls, LLM+rule judges grade the trace, auto-refine loop feeds failing rationales to claude -p; multiple configs prevent regressions.
quote: Multiple test configs can cover the same skill ... a fix that addresses one failing test config must not cause another to regress.

claim: Autonomous skill triggering is ~50% reliable; budget overflow silently truncates descriptions (SLASH_COMMAND_TOOL_CHAR_BUDGET); write 3 test cases before the body; UserPromptSubmit hook with explicit Use Skill() is deterministic.
quote: autonomous triggering achieves only roughly a 50% success rate because Claude prioritizes task completion over checking available tools.

claim: The description is the trigger (fuzzy-matched); overlapping descriptions cause non-deterministic wrong-skill selection; fix with explicit use-this-for-X-not-Y disambiguation and narrower domains.
quote: If two skills have overlapping descriptions you can get the wrong one ... the choice is non-deterministic enough to be a debugging nightmare.

claim: Skills 2.0 (April 2026): keep descriptions single-line or skills silently vanish; description budget ~1-2% of context; reasonable active set is 5-8 skills per project.
quote: a reasonable starting point, in my experience, is 5-8 active skills per project.
